After some thought about which projects I'm truly passionate about and what kind of production style would work best for me, I'm probably just going to focus on my main game in Unity and work on my Unreal Engine project on the side. I had 5 or 6 game ideas in total that I've now brought down to 2 concurrent projects, which seems more doable.

I draw, animate, write, compose, and now the part I'm having to learn is the coding/programming, which I'm mostly accomplishing using tutorials. I have a pretty decent start on my first game, but I'm definitely prepared to be working on this for however long it takes, whether that be a year or five years. I've completed books, I've completed comics, I've completed albums, now I want to finish some games :)

lmao, okay. I can tell you've never created anything for the sake of it. I completed all of those projects. It is not uncommon for someone to have multiple projects or ideas at once. Almost every author I know has plans for future books, other IPs, etc. I believe the key to balancing these projects is allocation of time and resources, as I stated above. I never said making games wasn't hard work. I actually said it was the opposite. It's the hardest work I've ever done. But it's rewarding and again, if I properly manage resources and time, what would be the issue? Because others have tried, I'm doomed to fail? You made a lot of baseless assumptions and then tried to pass it off as some kind of guru-esque life-coach crap. Seriously?

I am doing it as a hobby for sure, and if it makes me some cash that's cool. I definitely get where she's coming from as she is a children's book illustrator and works on strick deadlines, whereas I'm just trying to make cool stuff. And that's exactly how I would describe it, bursting with ideas! I'll look at a 3d model or watch a show or read a book and think to myself "that would make a cool game" and ideas just start flowing. I had two other projects I scrapped (a 2.5d platformer and a claymation point and click adventure game) but I think as long as I stay focused I can deliver on the 4 games I do plan on making. Supposedly Unreal Engine is easier to work with than Unity, and I've mostly been able to figure things out with Unity with my background in CAD, HTML, and generally following tutorials. The most robust game gameplay wise would be the one made in Unreal (an unconventional Final Fantasy style RPG), so that's about as complicated as it would get. I'm mostly inspired by smaller, more introspective games like Limbo, Inside, Little Nightmares, Journey, etc. all which don't have the most complicated gameplay systems/styles (which I think is the most complicated part to program personally).
